name: Meath

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Meath is the English name of the province Mide. Ancient Ireland had four provinces: Leinster, Munster, Connacht, and Ulster. Mide, or Meath, was the invisible fifth. The Indo-European world view placed a mysterious center point beyond the four physical districts. Mide was that spiritual center, a place not of this world. The word Mide means both neck and middle. It marked the point where the idea of the land's sovereignty joined the physical land. The joining took place on the hill of Uisneach, at the cracked boulder called the Stone of Divisions. A later county named Meath held the hill of Tara, the island's ancient political center.
